title: Trigonometry & Heights / Distances
intro: Trigonometry in SSC rests on three pillars: the ratios (sin, cos, tan and their reciprocals), the standard-angle table (0, 30, 45, 60, 90), and the identities. Memorise the table cold and most direct questions are instant evaluations. The identities sin^2 + cos^2 = 1, 1 + tan^2 = sec^2 and 1 + cot^2 = cosec^2 simplify the rest. Heights and distances then apply tan to a right triangle: tan(angle) = opposite/adjacent.

items.name: Basic ratios
items.formula: sin = opp/hyp, cos = adj/hyp, tan = opp/adj

items.name: Heights & distances
items.formula: tan(angle of elevation) = height / horizontal distance

topics.name: Trigonometric Ratios
topics.details: In a right triangle, for an acute angle: sine = opposite/hypotenuse, cosine = adjacent/hypotenuse, tangent = opposite/adjacent. The reciprocals are cosecant, secant and cotangent. Given one ratio you can reconstruct the triangle (using Pythagoras) and read off the others — for example, if sin = 3/5, the sides are 3, 4, 5 and cos = 4/5, tan = 3/4.

solved.problem: If sin A = 3/5, find cos A and tan A.
If tan A = 1, what is angle A (acute)?
If cos A = 12/13, find sin A.

topics.name: Standard Angle Values
topics.details: Lock in the table for 0, 30, 45, 60 and 90 degrees. sin runs 0, 1/2, 1/root2, root3/2, 1; cos is the reverse; tan = sin/cos. Most SSC direct questions are just substitutions from this table, so recalling it instantly is worth several marks per paper.

topics.name: Identities
topics.details: Three Pythagorean identities do most of the simplifying: sin^2 + cos^2 = 1, 1 + tan^2 = sec^2, and 1 + cot^2 = cosec^2. Rearrange them to swap between functions, and use them to prove or evaluate expressions. A common SSC move: replace sec^2 - tan^2 by 1, or 1 - sin^2 by cos^2, to collapse a long expression.

solved.problem: If sin A = 3/5, find sec A.

topics.name: Heights & Distances
topics.details: Model the situation as a right triangle: the angle of elevation (looking up) or depression (looking down) sits at the observer, the height is the opposite side and the ground distance the adjacent side, so tan(angle) = height/distance. Standard angles 30, 45, 60 give clean answers. For two observations, set up two equations and subtract.

solved.problem: The angle of elevation of a tower top from 30 m away is 45 degrees. Tower height?
From 20 m, the elevation of a pole top is 60 degrees. Height?
solved.solution: tan 60 = h/20 = root3 -> h = 20 root3 m.

solved.problem: A 15 m ladder leans at 60 degrees to the ground. Height it reaches?
solved.solution: sin 60 = h/15 -> h = 15 x root3/2 = 7.5 root3 m.

solved.problem: Elevation of a tower top is 30 degrees from 90 m. Height (use tan 30 = 1/root3)?

unsolved.problem: A 10 m ladder at 30 degrees reaches what height?
Shadow of a pole equals its height. Sun elevation?

shortcuts: Reconstruct a triangle from one ratio using Pythagorean triples (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17).
sec^2 - tan^2 = 1 and cosec^2 - cot^2 = 1 collapse long expressions.
Heights & distances: tan(angle) = height / ground distance.
mistakes: Swapping sin and cos values in the standard table.
Using sin instead of tan in elevation problems (tan = height/distance).
Dropping the square in sin^2 + cos^2 = 1.
pyq: SSC Tier 2 asks direct standard-angle evaluations, identity simplifications, and single/double-observation height-and-distance problems at 30/45/60.
summary: Know the ratios, the standard-angle table and the three Pythagorean identities by heart. Reconstruct triangles from a single ratio, simplify with the identities, and solve heights/distances with tan(angle) = height/distance.
